title: Dungeon
paragraphs: And so, we’ve arrived in the region of the country where the projectile weapon Seven Star Hero was reportedly sighted. After getting off the airship, we unloaded the carriage and had the Filolials pull it as we began our journey. The search area is quite large after all. Since the country also wants to locate the Seven Star Hero, they’re gathering information through the adventurer’s guild.
“What kind of country is this?”
“It was a country full of dungeons back when it was just a game.”
“Same for me, more or less.”
“Hmm…”
Father and the others gave their impressions while looking at the scenery from the carriage.
“What about you, Motoyasu?”
“It’s a country with many instant dungeons.”
I remember there were often recruitment calls near dungeons and at the capital, which served as a base. Of course, that’s from when it was a game.

“Dungeon exploration, huh… It does sound interesting, but searching for the Seven Star Hero is the priority. By the way, how are dungeons in this world?” Father asked the person who knew the hero’s face.
Éclair was also watching closely.
“Well… I’m not exactly an expert…”
“Are Iwatani-dono and the others asking what dungeons are like here, or are you asking how they differ from the ones you know?”
Éclair’s question made Father and the others furrow their brows in confusion. Is it such a difficult question?
“That’s a tough one. I think the best way to find out is to go in and see for yourself.”
“Yeah, that’s probably true. Should we check it out just in case?”
“Why not? Motoyasu, have you ever been inside a dungeon?”

I haven’t been in many, but I have entered a few dungeons. Even in this loop, just the other day, I went to retrieve bio-plant seeds for the physician. They were inside a treasure chest, so calling it a dungeon wouldn’t be inaccurate.
“I have, indeed.”
My response drew Father’s attention. Being stared at so much is embarrassing, I say.
“I don’t get why you’re blushing about that…”
“Quit being shy and explain.”
“The mechanisms were the same as in the game. However, unlike in games, monsters and traps didn’t respawn after re-entering multiple times.”

The mechanisms in the dungeon where the bio-plant was located only needed to be solved once. The monsters didn’t respawn after being defeated either. Well, since monsters are living creatures, maybe after a while, their numbers replenish. If you want to call that game-like, I guess it is, but unlike a game, things don’t instantly respawn upon re-entering.
“That means, depending on the item, normally… Ah!”
Father clapped his hands. Did he think of something?
“Is there any chance that treasure might regenerate in a dungeon after someone has already cleared it?”

Father’s words made Ren and Itsuki nod. Indeed, phrasing the question that way should provide the answer. In the game, since they were instant dungeons, resetting them caused the enemies and items to respawn. However, since this world isn’t exactly the same as the game, the outcome might be different.
“I see, that question should definitely tell us if there’s anything game-like going on here.”
“Yeah, honestly, I’ve been wondering if adventurers make a living doing more than just hunting bandits and slaying monsters. Maybe treasure hunting is part of it?”
When everyone turned to look at Éclair…
“I do know of some dungeons where treasure supposedly regenerates… but generally, I’ve never heard of treasures in ruins or dungeons reappearing.”
“Then that means it’s just a normal ruin in practical terms?”
“Maybe it’s a case of looters getting there first and leaving nothing behind?”
Éclair and the others nodded at Itsuki’s question. Well, that’s the logical conclusion. Even the bio-plant seeds I handed over to the physician were in a treasure chest, but I doubt they’ll respawn.
“So, it’s the same in another world, huh…”
“I heard that a lot of Egyptian treasures were looted too. In a way, maybe the roots of looting go back to that era.”
“Treasure hunting sounds exciting, but in reality, it’s just looting… In games, you’d usually find good weapons in treasure chests though…”

Exactly. If there’s a tough enemy in a difficult dungeon, it’s only natural that you’d expect to find good weapons, armor, and items as a reward. Well, in online games, even after defeating a strong boss, the drop rate for rare items wasn’t that high. How nostalgic. I remember grinding through instant dungeons repeatedly to get rare items. Of course, that was back in the game.

“Treasure hunting… In Brave Star Online, outside of quests, there was a time attack wave event, which was treated like the Waves here, where you’d explore a dungeon while fighting monsters. Clearing it would give you items as a result.”
“Anything else?”
“Other than that, it was just a monster nest.”
“Same for me. Outside of quests, it was just an instant dungeon where you could get rare items.”
“Well, that’s how it is… Maybe I was dreaming too much about adventure…”
Well, we were all a bunch of dreamers. It’s no wonder we admired dungeons like those in games. Oh? Itsuki raised his hand.
“In Dimension Wave, the game I played, there was definitely treasure.”
“Ah, that’s right. Your game was a console game, wasn’t it? In that case, it makes sense.”
“Once you took it, though, it didn’t respawn…”
“Wasn’t it more about monster drops instead?”
Father’s question made Itsuki nod. In the end, we’re all gamers.
“There are that many dungeons in this country?”
“Apparently, back when this country was a great nation, the king at the time built a lot of them to protect his treasures.”
“If it’s related to great nations, there might be some in Faubrey too.”
“That’s possible. After all, there were dungeons even in the game. The most famous one would be the underground waterways, right?”
“Isn’t there one in Melromarc too? I mean, I get that underground waterways being treated as dungeons makes sense as a gamer, but realistically, I doubt there’d be any treasure there…”
“If there’s anything down there, wouldn’t it be more likely to be remnants of a thief’s hideout rather than actual treasure?”

Ren’s comment made Father and Itsuki fall silent. That’s quite possible. Father seemed familiar with that kind of game and looked convinced. In games, do underground waterways usually mean thieves? Aside from Makai Daichi, the only other game I’ve played is Emerald Online, so I’m not too familiar with the concept.
“From a hero’s perspective, wouldn’t the real treasure be the drops from the monsters and bosses living in such places?”
“Exactly. That’s a privilege unique to heroes.”
“During the activation event on Cal Mira Island, there are exclusive drops, after all. In a way, that place is also like a dungeon.”
Father mentioned that he obtained the material for a Filolial costume there. So, when the activation period comes around again, I definitely want to go and get it.
“That activation… isn’t that more like a time-limited event in an online game? You know, the kind of events that game developers set up for summer vacation, Christmas, or New Year’s?”
“Yeah, that’s exactly right. The old me would’ve been talking about double experience events and limited-time quests back then.”

Exactly. Online games usually have events tied to the seasons. In the first world, I remember being super excited, thinking it was one of those limited-time events Ren mentioned. Itsuki seems a little unsure, but it looks like his game had similar events. In console games, it would be more like a bonus stage or something like that.
“It’s kind of sad how we’re all just accepting that.”
“Wait, what were we talking about again?”
“Ah, right. I was asking if this country’s economy runs on dungeons.”

“I’ve heard that there are dungeons here and there that no one has ever explored to the lowest levels. It’s turned into a kind of tourist attraction for adventurers and martial artists. Apparently, rookie adventurers go there to gain experience.”
“They probably have entrance fees, health insurance, and even rescue teams that come if you sound an alarm before the third floor.”
What kind of attraction is this?
“Don’t say something so blunt.”
“Yeah, Naofumi.”
Father’s comment made Ren and Itsuki retort. Oh? Éclair averted her gaze. Then she muttered quietly.
“…There is.”
